new_statements.translation: The accent is in the main the same as in Dutch and High German. [p. 100] ... In general the vowels, when they do not carry the stress, lose a part, but a very small one, of their duration and timbre. [...] With diphthongs the stress falls on the first element. [p. 101]

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (140 scan pages, KB/Delpher urn MMKB02:000125611) via the page scan and and the text lines 6656-6790). Printed p. 100 (Afdeeling II, §159 'Articulatiebasis of stand van den mond', which starts on p. 99 and runs to the foot of p. 100) reads verbatim: 'Het accent is in hoofdzaak hetzelfde als in het Nederlandsch en het Hoogduitsch.' (one sentence, between 'De medeklinkers zijn altijd kort en ongespannen.' and 'Alle medeklinkerverbindingen voor of na een klinker zijn glijderloos (glideless) behalve kn.'). Printed p. 101, under the heading 'Timbre, duur en accent', §162, reads verbatim: 'Over het algemeen verliezen de klinkers, als zij niet den klem hebben, een gedeelte, maar een zeer kl…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Eijkman gives no explicit placement rule of his own; he states that word accent is essentially the Dutch/High German (Germanic) pattern, i.e. main stress on the root/stem syllable, which is word-initial in native simplex words, with unstressed prefixes (his transcriptions: fa'jetn 'vergeten', ba'toNkja 'bedank', fceir'bi 'voorbij' vs. 'kaikalp, 'alagera). Spenter 1971 independently refers to 'unbetonte Vorsilben' and a loan with non-initial stress (s'rin 'Rosine'). Diphthongs are falling (stress on the first element).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated as exceptions; loanwords with non-initial stress appear in the data (Spenter 1971: s'rin 'Rosine'; Eijkman's transcription fceir'bi 'voorbij').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement made by comparison with Dutch and German, inside a phonetic (instrumental + auditory) description; stress marked in sentence and word transcriptions, not treated as a separate topic.
new_statements.identity_note: Eijkman 1925 describes the Frisian of the island of Schiermonnikoog itself (schi1234; no dialect subdivisions), from fieldwork on the island in 1913 with instrumental recordings and native informants; the same variety as Fokkema's and Spenter's 'Schiermonnikoogs/Schiermonnikooger Mundart'. Glottolog dates Fokkema's sketch 1969 but the KB catalogue records it as 1959/1960 (Fedde Dijkstra, Leeuwarden).

sources.note: p. 100 (§159): 'Het accent is in hoofdzaak hetzelfde als in het Nederlandsch en het Hoogduitsch' (stress essentially as in Dutch and German); p. 101 (§162 'Timbre, duur en accent'): diphthongs are falling, stress on their first element; unstressed vowels lose a little duration/timbre; transcriptions pp. 110ff mark stress (') with prefixes unstressed (fa'jetn 'vergeten', ba'toNkja 'bedank') and root/stem stressed.
